summary: This CSS defines an animated element called 'runner' that slides across the screen from left to right over 3 seconds. It's positioned off-screen initially, made non-interactive with pointer-events, and includes an accessibility consideration to disable the animation for users who prefer reduced motion.

explanations.2: position: fixed means this element stays in place relative to the viewport (the window you're looking at), rather than moving when you scroll.
explanations.4: left: -160px positions the element 160 pixels to the left of the screen edge, so it starts completely off-screen and out of view.
explanations.8: pointer-events: none makes the element invisible to mouse clicks and touches — clicks pass right through it to whatever's underneath.
explanations.9: animation: run-across 3s linear forwards tells the element to use the 'run-across' animation, taking 3 seconds, moving at a constant speed, and staying at its final position when done.
explanations.17: left: 100vw means move the element to 100% of the viewport width (all the way across the screen to the right edge).
explanations.21: This media query detects if a user has enabled 'reduce motion' accessibility settings in their OS, and if so, we respect that preference.
explanations.24: Instead of animating, just place it in the middle (50vw) so users with motion sensitivity still see the element but without the movement.
